rust_crates_dependencies.note: Direct [dependencies] in the vendored Cargo.toml files: harpe: none; kibisis: none; argus-ledger: ed25519-dalek, getrandom, serde_json, sha2.

network_code.note: No socket, HTTP or process-spawn API found in the vendored source of the three crates (5 .rs files, regex search). Dependencies are not scanned.

kibisis_cipher.value: AES-256-GCM entry encryption; SQLCipher whole-file encryption when sqlcipher3 is installed
kibisis_cipher.note: Python kibisis at v0.1.0-alpha.4 (src/kibisis/crypto.py and vault.py): entry content is encrypted with AES-256-GCM under a key derived with PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 (600,000 iterations for new envelopes). With the sqlcipher3 module the package declares, SQLCipher also encrypts the whole database file; without it the vault opens with plain SQLite pages. The Rust kibisis crate keeps its vault and lease coordinator in memory and has no encryption implementation.

argus_structure.value: Linear SHA-256 hash chain with optional Ed25519 signatures on event hashes
argus_structure.note: Argus uses a strictly linear SHA-256 hash chain where each event hash covers sequence, id, timestamp, type, actor, prev_hash and the SHA-256 digest of the payload.

harpe_algorithm.note: Pinned items first, then remaining items in priority order while budget remains. Deterministic; not an optimal 0/1 knapsack packing.

retired.claim: Higher token-reduction and lower per-turn time (84.77% / 24.3 µs) plus dollar savings
retired.why: The committed report (step1_knapsack_cost_curve.json) shows 78.29% and 60.53 µs/turn. Dollar figures depend on assumed provider pricing and are omitted from headline claims.

retired.claim: Argus instant tamper detection in tens of microseconds
retired.why: The 42 µs figure was an early abort near genesis. Reaching an edit at sequence 500,000 in a 1,000,000 event ledger takes 219.34 ms (step3_argus_1m_scale.json).
Argus is a linear SHA-256 hash chain. Described as that accurately across all surfaces.
Harpe uses deterministic priority-ordered greedy selection, not an exact 0/1 integer programming solver.

retired.claim: Zero-allocation steady state; zero garbage collection
retired.why: Harpe allocates context items. Absence of garbage collection is an inherent Rust property, not a library feature.

retired.claim: CMMC Level 2, NIST SP 800-53, or ATO ready
retired.why: No independent security or compliance assessment has been completed. The libraries are designed for local and disconnected use.
PGP key was not published on keys.openpgp.org. Removed until key publication.

retired.claim: Values, medians and ranges typed into scripts/build_claims.py
retired.why: Up to v0.1.0-alpha.4 they were typed in from single runs at ca3dff7 and not checked against reports/. Each value is now read from reports/; a single run has no median or range.

retired.claim: Rust and Python test counts (36 and 135)
retired.why: Typed in and not recounted; the per-crate Rust counts given (4, 11 and 23) sum to 38. Each library repository's CI runs its own tests.
True for harpe only. Direct dependencies in the vendored Cargo.toml files: argus-ledger 4.

retired.claim: Reports generated on dedicated pinned performance cores
retired.why: The benchmark machine is a shared server, not an isolated one: taskset keeps the programs on their CPUs but does not keep other processes off them.

retired.claim: Single-bit history corruption trapped at sequence 500,000
retired.why: The program replaces the payload of event 500,000; it does not flip a single bit.

retired.claim: SIGSTOP fault injection in the multi-process test
retired.why: The pause past the TTL is simulated with a sleep; no SIGSTOP signal is sent.

retired.claim: SQLCipher page-level encryption with PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 (600,000 iterations)
retired.why: The 600,000-iteration PBKDF2 derives the AES-256-GCM key for entry content. SQLCipher encrypts the whole file only when the sqlcipher3 module is installed.
